body: claimed: issue-worker-medium · 2026-11-12T13:46Z · worktree/branch issue/1206-setup-machine-post-per-setup · plan: reproduce per-setup machine/post picks in a two-setup UI test, then fix the missing or wrong step

Reproduction (UI test, two setups, base origin/main 62a2c93a), before any fix:

- Setup2's Machine page (browser node, which activates Setup2 first): the radio "This setup has its own machine" is present and sets Setup2's own machine; Setup1 stays on the document's (no own machine).
- Setup2's Machine page Library picker ("Lathe") routes to Setup2's own machine, Setup1 untouched.
- Setup2's Post page: the radio "This setup has its own post" and the post picker ("Fanuc" -> "Haas") set Setup2's own post; Setup1 and the document keep theirs.
- Full flow (Setup2 on Tilt-head 5-axis with Haas, Setup1 on the document's VMC 3-axis with Fanuc, one face each): post_mounts writes two files, each carrying its own mount's post.

So no missing or wrong step reproduced in the Setup pages on this base: every control exists, is wired to the setup's own command, and the program posts one file per mount. What I could not reproduce: the failing path the maintainer hit. Candidates not yet driven: a page opened from the Setups page or ribbon rather than the browser node, the post picker on a lathe/mill-turn setup, and the "Load post (.cps)" route. Not a cross-setup post or machine leak, so the P1 escalation does not apply.

What the branch will carry: the pinned tests (regression pins, they pass on main), no product change yet. The PR will say Refs #1206 so the issue stays open until the failing path is found.

fix on issue/1206-setup-machine-post-per-setup · PR #1222 · pinned by each_setup_picks_its_own_machine_and_post_and_posts_one_file_per_mount, the_setup_machine_page_takes_its_own_machine, the_setup_machine_page_picks_its_own_machine_from_the_library, the_setup_post_page_takes_its_own_post_through_the_picker · regression pins only (the failing path is not found yet, PR says Refs) · merges when reviewed

Maintainer's answer (question dialog, 2026-11-12) to "where did you try to pick them when it didn't work?": **"The setup's own Machine/Post page"** - on Setup<n> > Machine or Post the controls were missing, greyed out or did not stick.

So the path is the per-setup pages themselves, and PR #1222's pins (which pass on main) do not cover the state he was in. Still to probe, most likely first:
1. **An inactive setup's page.** A plain click on a setup's browser node opens its page WITHOUT making it active (`browser_pane.rs`), and other per-setup pages then show only "<name> is not the active setup - activate it ..." (found today in the review of PR #1211 for the Fixtures page). Open Setup2 > Machine and Setup2 > Post by plain browser clicks while Setup1 is active: are the radios and pickers there, enabled, and do they write to Setup2 (not to the active setup, not to the document)?
2. **One setup only**, and the implicit "Setup" of a document with no setups.
3. **Does not stick:** pick, then switch setups / open another page / save and reopen the project / undo-redo - is the pick still shown and still used at post time?
4. **Machine kinds:** a lathe or mill-turn setup next to a mill setup (the post picker lists only posts that serve the machine - is the list empty or the pick refused silently?), and "Load post (.cps)" on a setup.

More from the maintainer (chat, 2026-11-12): "When u select a machine or post processor on one sub-setups pages it changes on both sub-setups pages.. its likely a single registration for what machine and posts in the Overarching setup page that is propagated thru out all sub-setups".

That narrows it: the pick made on Setup<n> > Machine / Post lands on the shared (document) mount, so every setup that follows the document shows it too. The model has both states by design (`setup_mount.rs`: a setup owns its mount, or follows the document's), and PR #1222's pins all switch the setup to "own machine" / "own post" first - which is why they pass. The path he took is the other one: **picking in the list while the setup still follows the document** (the default for every setup), which edits the document's machine/post and so changes all setups at once.

To reproduce first (expected to FAIL on main): two setups, both untouched (following the document). On Setup2 > Machine pick another machine from the picker without touching the own/follow radio; same on Setup2 > Post. Assert what the maintainer expects: Setup2 has the new machine/post, Setup1 and the document keep theirs.

Fix direction (decide and record): a pick made on a setup's own page is a pick FOR THAT SETUP - it makes the setup own its mount in the same undoable step - while "follow the document" stays an explicit choice on that page that shows which machine/post it follows; the document-wide machine and post are changed only where the page says "document" (the overarching Setups / document page, the ribbon), never as a side effect of a setup page. Check the ribbon's machine door and the Setups overview against the same rule and say on each control whose mount it changes.

Rating stays P3 for now (he sees both pages change, so it is visible). If the reproduction shows a setup POSTING through a post it does not display, or generated against a machine it does not display, re-rate P1.

claimed: issue-worker-medium · 2026-11-12T14:17Z · worktree/branch issue/1206-setup-machine-post-per-setup (fresh worktree issue-1206b) · plan: reproduce the document-following pick on Setup2 pages as failing tests, then make a setup's own-page pick own its mount in one undoable step

Closed as not a bug - the maintainer, 2026-11-12: "if i tick the box 'this setup has its own machine' - it works. the bug is wrongly reported". The behaviour is as designed (#343): a setup follows the document's machine and post until its own-machine / own-post box is ticked; a pick made while it follows the document changes the document's pair for every setup that follows it. No code change. PR #1222 keeps the four regression pins for the per-setup picks (test-only, `Refs`).
